verdictReason: The 19 tests are well-written and all pass, and the integration test genuinely proves zero-token/pin behavior. But the false-positive hunt (weighted most important) found that 4 of 10 realistic legit Hot Wheels news snippets (official Mattel Creations store drop with member discount, Mattel's own storefront-relaunch news, a hobby shop closing, a PT restock piece) are silently blocked by the current rule. All four share one root cause: the URL-path token bonus ('loja'/'shop'/'store' in the slug counts as STRONG) combines with completely ordinary commerce vocabulary that legitimate autoevolution/lamley/mattel/t-hunted headlines routinely use. Recommend tuning before shipping, or accepting the tradeoff explicitly and adding regression tests that pin the current false-positive cases as known/accepted.

TestIsPromoArticle.notes: Meaningful, real-assertion tests (no mock-only checks). Good coverage of the scoring rule's documented boundaries: 2-STRONG-via-url-token blocks, 1 STRONG + 2 WEAK blocks, 1 STRONG + 1 WEAK does not, a single STRONG never blocks, weak-only (any count) never blocks. Accent/case folding is genuinely exercised (the 'nao perca' ASCII variant forces NFKD-fold to matter, not just a same-string round-trip). Scan-bound tests (paragraph count and char cap) are correct and match the implementation's slicing order. Crash-safety test covers None entry/article and empty/missing paragraphs, matching the documented contract.

TestPromoBlockedAlert.notes: Verifies real message content (title, link, every matched marker, the 'Отсечена реклама' substring anchor used by the integration test, plain-text-only formatting) rather than just checking the function was called. Empty-markers case checks no 'None' leaks into the rendered text.

TestIntakeFunnel (promo additions).notes: test_collapse_note_promo_dominant and test_funnel_line_counts_promo_in_dropped both assert on rendered string content, not implementation details. Correctly show promo folded into both the per-stage bullet and the compact 'отсеяно' sum.

TestPromoIntakeFilter.notes: Real SQLite, real job() run. Genuinely proves the zero-token/pre-translation claim: pending_articles count stays 0 and get_pending() is None for the link (translation only ever operates on rows in pending_articles, confirmed by reading job()'s later staging code, so this is real proof, not an assumption). Proves exactly one [E035] admin call fires and no E014/E015 fires for the same drop. Proves the mark_processed pin works operationally, not just that mark_processed was called: it resets the fetch_full_article mock and runs job() a second time, asserting fetch_full_article is never called again for that link — this is the strongest evidence in the whole diff and correctly targets the real regression risk (daily re-fetch/re-alert spam).

findings.title: URL-token STRONG bonus + ordinary commerce vocabulary silently drops real news
findings.detail: 4 of 10 realistic snippets modeled on plausible autoevolution/lamley/mattel/t-hunted content were blocked: an official Mattel Creations store-drop-with-member-discount announcement, a news piece about Mattel relaunching its own online store, a hobby shop closing after 30 years (community news, not an ad), and a PT restock roundup. In every case the trigger was 1 STRONG marker supplied by the URL-path token bonus ('store'/'shop'/'loja' in the slug) combined with 1-2 ordinary WEAK/STRONG words a journalist would naturally use ('discount', 'in stock', 'on sale', 'free shipping', or an incidental 'shop now offers' word sequence). None of these are ad copy — they are exactly the kind of coverage this channel's actual sources publish about Mattel Creations drops, retail exclusives, and community shop news. See falsePositiveProbe array for verbatim snippets and matched markers.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) demote the URL-token bonus from STRONG to WEAK so a slug containing 'store'/'shop'/'loja' alone can no longer complete the bar together with just one more incidental weak word, or (b) require 2 independent body-text STRONG markers before the URL token can contribute, or (c) if the team accepts this tradeoff (better to over-block than under-block, per the '[E035] false positive → report it, patterns get tuned' operator workflow already built into the alert), add these four cases as explicit regression tests documenting the accepted tradeoff so it's a decision, not a blind spot.

findings.title: Word-boundary claim ('loja' must not match 'lojas', 'store' must not match 'restored') has no regression test that would actually fail if the guard broke
findings.detail: Verified directly: fold('loja') is NOT a substring of fold('lojas'), and fold('store') is NOT a substring of fold('restored') — the implementation is correct today. But the only existing negative test that mentions 'lojas' (test_pt_news_chega_as_lojas_not_blocked) contains zero STRONG markers in its fixture, so `len(strong) >= 2 or (strong and len(weak) >= 2)` is False purely because `strong` is empty — the test would still pass unchanged even if the word-boundary guard were completely removed and 'loja' started matching inside 'lojas'. No test in the suite uses the word 'restored' at all (grepped tests/test_relevance_filter.py — zero hits), despite this exact case being called out in the module docstring and in this review's focus list.
findings.recommendation: Add a dedicated test pairing a genuine STRONG marker with a plural/compound word that would trip a naive substring matcher if the boundary logic regressed, e.g. 1 STRONG ('compre já') + body text containing only 'lojas' (plural) and 'restored'-like filler, asserting the result stays under the bar specifically because 'loja'/'store' do NOT match inside those words — not just that the overall verdict happens to be False for unrelated reasons.

findings.title: _is_promo_article call site in job() is not wrapped in try/except, unlike the dedup gate
findings.detail: A non-string `entry['link']` (e.g. int or list — possible from a malformed/Atom-style feed) crashes `_is_promo_article` via `urlparse(entry.get('link') or '')`. This is NOT a regression introduced by this diff: `fetch_full_article`, called earlier in the same loop iteration on the same field, already does `urlparse(entry.get('link') or '')` unguarded, so a malformed link already crashes the tick before promo filtering is ever reached. Documenting for awareness only — not a defect specific to this change, and not blocking.
findings.recommendation: No action required for this diff. If the team ever hardens `fetch_full_article` against non-string links, extend the same guard to `_is_promo_article` at the same time.

findings.title: Integration test's re-fetch proof is the strongest test in the diff
findings.detail: test_promo_article_dropped_at_intake resets the fetch_full_article mock and re-runs job(), then asserts assert_not_called() — this is a real operational proof that the processed_news pin prevents next-tick re-fetch, not just a check that mark_processed() was invoked with the right arguments. Worth calling out as a pattern to reuse for other pin-on-drop features.
